record.paper_title: Problems in Data Structures and Algorithms
record.context_brief: static optimal BST with internal nodes
record.original_question: Let w1, w2, ..., wn be positive weights on n ordered items, and consider binary search trees that store the items in their internal nodes, with the i-th item appearing in symmetric order at depth di. What is the fastest algorithm for constructing a tree minimizing Σ_i w_i d_i? In particular, can the classical O(n^2) dynamic-programming bound be improved, and can any nontrivial lower bound be proved for this optimization problem?

evidence.quote: Problem 6.1 Items can be stored in the internal nodes of the tree. ... Given positive weights w1, w2,...,wn, construct an n-node binary tree that minimizes n i=1 widi , where di is the depth of the i-th node in symmetric order.

Here we have an O(n2) dynamic programming algorithm with a certain amount of cleverness in it. This result is twenty-five years old or so. Nothing better is known. There may, in fact, be a faster algorithm for Problem 6.1; no nontrivial lower bound for the problem is known.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n be a positive integer and let w_1, w_2, ..., w_n be positive real weights associated with n items given in a fixed linear order. Consider rooted binary trees with exactly n internal nodes into which the n items are placed at the internal nodes so that an in-order (symmetric-order) traversal lists the items in their given order. For such a tree T, let d_i denote the depth of the node holding item i (the root has depth 1, or equivalently 0; fix one convention). Define the cost of T to be C(T) = sum_{i=1}^n w_i d_i.

(a) Design the asymptotically fastest possible algorithm that, given w_1, ..., w_n, constructs a tree T* minimizing C(T). In particular, determine whether the classical O(n^2)-time dynamic programming algorithm for this problem can be improved to o(n^2) time.

(b) Prove any nontrivial (superlinear) lower bound on the time complexity of this problem in a reasonable model of computation.
artifact.status_search_result: Knuth's 1971 O(n^2) dynamic programming algorithm for constructing the statically optimal binary search tree (with items at internal nodes) remains the best known exact algorithm; no faster exact algorithm and no nontrivial superlinear lower bound appear to be known. Faster algorithms exist only for approximate/nearly-optimal versions (e.g., Mehlhorn's linear-time approximation). The problem of beating O(n^2) for the exact version, or proving a lower bound, appears to still be open.

status_evidence.title: Optimal binary search tree - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Knuth's dynamic programming algorithm constructs the statically optimal tree in O(n^2) time. Mehlhorn introduced a simpler algorithm that closely approximates the optimal tree in O(n) time.
status_evidence.claim: O(n^2) remains the standard exact bound; only approximations are faster.

status_evidence.title: Comparing Implementations of Optimal Binary Search Trees
status_evidence.snippet: Knuth's algorithm runs in O(n^2) time; heuristics and approximations achieve O(n log n) or O(n).
status_evidence.claim: No improvement over O(n^2) for the exact problem is reported.
